candidate.title: CLASH-Seq
candidate.scope: The single linear CLASH-Seq schematic assigned to the Illumina card. CLASH-Seq is the catalogue label for CLASH (cross-linking, ligation, and sequencing of hybrids). The depicted route is protein-associated RNA duplex A/B, UV crosslinking, affinity purification, end ligation, and reverse transcription to cDNA. No alternative branch or other target method is drawn. The transient RNA:cDNA pair is represented within reverse transcription. The catalogue explains sequencing of the cDNA, but no sequencing, adapter-preparation, or amplification operation is depicted. This is a schematic architecture, not a complete implementation or laboratory recipe.

states.label: RNA duplex associated with a protein
features: Two RNA partners, brown A and purple B, form the depicted RNA duplex.
The blue oval is interpreted as the protein component using the card description; no particular bait protein or specimen is specified in the image.
A and B identify RNA partners, not barcodes or chemically specified ends.

operations.label: UV crosslinking
operations.description: UV exposure changes the initially associated RNA-protein complex into the depicted crosslinked complex; A and B remain present.
operations.mechanism: UV-induced crosslinking of RNA-protein complexes, as stated by the catalogue. The UV lightning symbol is an exposure cue, not an additional material branch.
operations.information_effect: Stabilizes protein association of the duplex for recovery; this step does not yet concatenate A and B sequences.

operations.label: Affinity purification
operations.description: Enriches the crosslinked RNA-protein complex from the starting material, producing the purified complex that proceeds to RNA ligation.
operations.mechanism: Protein-directed affinity purification; the specific bait, tag, affinity surface, and compartment are not given by the schematic.
operations.information_effect: Selects protein-associated recoverable RNA complexes. The represented interactions are constrained by the bait and recovery, rather than being a complete inventory of RNA duplexes.

operations.label: Ligate ends
operations.description: Joins ends of the two associated RNA partners in the purified complex, changing two RNA chains into a chimeric RNA carrying sequence from A and B. The source keeps the protein oval visible in the ligated icon.
operations.mechanism: RNA end ligation, with no enzyme, end polarity, or linker specified in the supplied schematic.
operations.information_effect: Converts the RNA-RNA association into sequence adjacency within a single RNA molecule, providing the template for a chimeric cDNA.

evidence.quote: Here, we describe a high-throughput method to identify intramolecular and intermolecular RNA-RNA interactions experimentally by cross-linking, ligation, and sequencing of hybrids (CLASH).
evidence.rationale: The primary abstract names CLASH and its hybrid-based readout. It does not provide a full protocol or independently specify all depicted chemistry.

operations.label: Reverse transcription
operations.description: Copies the ligated RNA hybrid into cDNA. The drawing summarizes this as a joined brown/purple RNA above a blue DNA strand, followed by the final cDNA-only strand. The card reports isolation of the ligated RNA before copying; the unshown isolation and template-removal chemistry are not separately reconstructed.
operations.mechanism: Reverse transcription of the ligated RNA template. The schematic does not specify primer design or how the protein and RNA template are removed from the final product.
operations.information_effect: Transfers the joined A/B sequence association from RNA into the DNA readout carrier. Chimeric sequences can identify the represented interacting RNA regions. Recovery and ligation do not by themselves guarantee that every chimera is a specific biological interaction.
